review: 1:1–1:2 is Psalm 119:105 verbatim (נֵר־לְרַגְלִי דְבָרֶךָ וְאוֹר לִנְתִיבָתִי); the Arabic سِرَاجٌ لِرِجْلِي كَلَامُكَ is that verse, and the stanza is only two lines in the print, so the whole verse fits.
2:2 הוּא מוֹרִי — 'He is my teacher/guide'; the participle of ירה in the hiph'il ('to instruct') is biblical (Ex 15:25), and it carries هُدَايَ ('my guidance').
3:1 זָהֳרִי — 'my radiance'; the noun זֹהַר is biblical (Ezek 8:2, Dan 12:3), used for ضِيَاء.

4:1–4:2 עָזְרֵנִי לִצְפֹּן / דְּבָרְךָ — 'help me to store up Your word'; the Arabic أُخَبِّئَنَّ is 'hide', and צָפַן is the verb of Ps 119:11 (צָפַנְתִּי אִמְרָתְךָ בְלִבִּי), which is the verse behind the stanza.
